answer: Reputation can depend on repeated work confirmed by several independent peers, whose endorsements count only if they have durable histories of their own. A new identity starts at nadir, with no trust to transfer. To gain influence, an attacker must fund accounts, do useful work, and sustain coordinated relationships over time. A trellis of cross-checks makes a cheap swarm ineffective; each fake account costs labor or resources, while the ember of reputation grows slowly.
